summary:
Dependency-ordered task list for TGP Phase 3 (Materials & light), covering registered PBR materials (material.add metal-roughness), hardened PNG/GLB-embedded texture decode with max_tex_dim/max_texels caps, punctual Light nodes with per-viewport replace-not-augment semantics + deterministic over-cap selection, per-viewport tone-map (Reinhard/ACES/none over the whole linear target), per-viewport MSAA with clamp-down + ack-report and the always-1x pick invariant, the sRGB-wire/linear-internal/sRGB-encode color pipeline, theme-tint as a pre-lighting default-material-input stage, and VRAM accounting for MSAA+resolve+pick targets.

ALL deliverables live in the greenfield TGP module trees (crates/toastty-graphics/src/tgp/* and crates/toastty-render/src/tgp/*) parallel to the legacy rgp/ — never reused (G8). The legacy crates/toastty-graphics/src/rgp/glb_loader.rs (first-primitive, no-texture) is NOT touched; TGP has its own hardened loader from P1 that P3 extends for embedded PNG.

TESTING SEAMS used: INGRESS (Parser::advance(&mut Term, bytes) → &self accessors: Term::tgp_scene() nodes/materials/textures, scene_revision/asset_revision, per-node/per-viewport dirty flags, viewport effective render opts, computed VRAM, pty_replies bytes); INTERACTION (synthetic pointer events via Term input API for the pick-vs-1x invariant); LIFECYCLE (RIS as bytes). Every test states concrete input bytes/events and the concrete accessor+expected value. The cross-crate apc_end back-channel (perform.rs:42 unit → ApcEnd) was established in P1 and is unchanged here; P3 binary frames (textures embedded in asset.add GLB, large material/texture patches) ride the existing enc=bin path, so each material/texture task includes an enc=bin variant test asserting the binary-frame path agrees with b64.

CROSS-PHASE DEPENDS (assumed delivered): P1 = TGP scene model, Term::tgp_scene(), dirty-flag/revision machinery, default material (MaterialId 0), CBOR patch decode, handshake/tgp;r/caps emit, viewport pixel rects, injectable clock, CPU world matrices, hardened TGP GLB loader (full mesh set). P2 = multiple viewports, instancing, CPU pick buffer + pick pass, sub/events, explore controller.

Every protocol surface in §11 gets at least one unit test: ops (material.add, asset.add fmt=png, node.upsert{material}, node.upsert{light}), header/field surfaces (model=pbr, base/metallic/rough/normal/emissive/occlusion, tex_* refs, render.msaa, render.tone_map, render.theme_tint, render.keep_default_light), error codes (parse_error detail=tex_dim|tex_format, cap_exceeded detail=max_tex_dim|max_texels_per_texture|max_lights_per_viewport, vram_exhausted, bad_ref tex:<id>, unsupported), caps (max_tex_dim, max_texels_per_texture, max_lights_per_viewport, msaa, color=srgb), and lifecycle events (cap_exceeded one-time-per-viewport light over-cap; RIS teardown of materials/textures/MSAA targets).

Add a single canonical entry point WireColor::linearize() applied ON INPUT to every color field. crates/toastty-render/src/tgp/target.rs (new): ViewportColorTarget describing the offscreen as a linear-DATA UNORM format (NOT *_SRGB auto-encoding) plus an explicit in-shader sRGB-encode stage marker; pub fn color_target_format()->wgpu::TextureFormat returning a non-sRGB UNORM. tasks.title: Hardened PNG decoder: header-first dimension check vs max_tex_dim, bounded decode vs max_texels_per_texture
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-graphics/src/tgp/texture.rs (new): pub fn decode_png(bytes:&[u8], caps)->Result<DecodedTexture, TexError>. ONE hardened PNG decoder (the only texture path in v1). Reads IHDR width/height FROM THE HEADER BEFORE full decode; if either axis > max_tex_dim → TexError::DimExceeded. If width*height > max_texels_per_texture → TexError::TexelsExceeded. Decode is bounded by the decode/parse-time cap (§15.2/§15.5) to guard decompression bombs: running output checked incrementally, abort + free partial on overflow. DecodedTexture { width, height, rgba8:Vec<u8> } stored sRGB on the wire (linearized at sample time / via texture format choice). TexError maps: DimExceeded→(parse_error, detail=tex_dim) for hard-reject AND cap_exceeded;detail=max_tex_dim for the cap locus — follow §11.2 wording: a texture exceeding max_tex_dim is rejected with parse_error detail=tex_dim. Expose nothing GPU.

tests.assert: decode_png returns DecodedTexture{width:2,height:2,rgba8.len()==16}

tests.name: png_over_max_tex_dim_rejected_from_header

tests.assert: returns TexError::DimExceeded BEFORE decoding IDAT (no full decompress attempted)

tests.name: png_over_max_texels_rejected

tests.name: png_decompression_bomb_bounded

tests.assert: decode aborts with a cap error and the partial allocation is freed (no unbounded growth)

tests.name: non_png_magic_rejected

tasks.title: asset.add fmt=png op: register a PNG texture asset; non-PNG byte asset → parse_error detail=tex_format
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-graphics/src/tgp/patch.rs + texture.rs: handle asset.add op with fmt="png" → route bytes through P3-T5 decoder, register a TextureAsset in the asset table keyed by (token, asset id u32). A non-PNG byte asset declared fmt=png (or any non-PNG fmt routed to the texture path) → x;code=parse_error;detail=tex_format, rejecting the WHOLE txn atomically (§8.6). A texture over max_tex_dim → x;code=parse_error;detail=tex_dim (whole-txn reject). asset.add commit bumps asset_revision once. Works under chunked asset.add (more=1/0) per §8.7 since textures can exceed one frame. Expose Term::tgp_texture(token, id)->Option<{width,height}>.

tasks.title: node.upsert{material} binding + bad_ref tex resolution within txn
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-graphics/src/tgp/patch.rs: node.upsert with material:<id> binds a Mesh/Instanced node to a registered MaterialId (committed-only ref, order-independent within txn per §8.6). material:null clears back to default (MaterialId 0). A material ref to an uncommitted/missing id → x;code=bad_ref;detail=material:<id>, whole-txn reject citing first offending op. A material's tex_* ref to an uncommitted/missing texture asset → x;code=bad_ref;detail=tex:<id>. Cross-token material/texture reference → x;code=denied;detail=token (§15.2). Setting material on a node bumps scene_revision + the node's transform/material dirty flag (NOT asset_revision). Expose the bound material id via Term::tgp_scene() node accessor (node.material_id()).

Kind-immutability per §8.6: a later upsert implying a different kind → x;code=kind_conflict. Expose Term::tgp_scene() node .light_data() and confirm Light nodes get a computed WORLD matrix like any node (so a parented headlight's world direction is queryable CPU-side).

tasks.title: Per-viewport effective light set + replace-not-augment switch (per visible subtree)
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-render/src/tgp/lighting.rs (new, CPU-side selection — GPU consumes) + crates/toastty-term viewport accessor: compute the effective light set for a viewport per frame from its visible subtree (the viewport's root subtree, defaulting to whole scene). If that set contains ≥1 Light node, the built-in key+ambient+hemisphere is DISABLED for that viewport (replace-not-augment, §11.3) and default-material nodes are lit only by registered lights through the same forward loop. Two viewports sharing one scene differ when their roots include/exclude the light. Expose Term::tgp_viewport_lighting(vp_id) → { registered_lights:Vec<NodeId>, default_light_active:bool } computed CPU-side without a GPU.

tasks.title: render.keep_default_light flag (additive fill) + deterministic over-cap light selection
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-render/src/tgp/lighting.rs + viewport RenderOpts: render.keep_default_light (default false) keeps the built-in key+ambient+hemisphere on ADDITIVELY alongside registered lights. Over-cap selection: when the effective set exceeds max_lights_per_viewport, DETERMINISTICALLY select the N highest-intensity lights (by light.intensity scalar; ties broken by ASCENDING node-id lexicographic order) and ignore the rest for that frame — never crash, never nondeterministic. The over-cap patch is NOT rejected (animated lights). Expose the selected/dropped split through Term::tgp_viewport_lighting so tests assert the deterministic choice.

tasks.title: One-time-per-viewport cap_exceeded latch for light over-cap (lifecycle event)
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-term/src/tgp/lighting_latch.rs (new) + viewport state: going over max_lights_per_viewport queues a ONE-TIME-PER-VIEWPORT x;code=cap_exceeded;detail=max_lights_per_viewport, routed only to the owning token and only if that token handshaked (§7/§15.3). The latch clears (and may re-fire once) when the visible light count drops back under cap. The over-cap patch itself still commits (T11). Expose Term::tgp_viewport_light_latch(vp)->bool for test assertion. Latch transitions evaluated per frame against the deterministic injectable clock / render tick.

tests.assert: latch==false after the drop; then a SECOND cap_exceeded is queued on re-exceeding (re-fire once)

tests.assert: no tgp;x emitted (gated on handshake); scene still safe (lights selected deterministically)

tasks.title: Theme-tint: render.theme_tint flag + pre-lighting default-material-input stage (default-material, neutral-tint nodes only)
tasks.deliverable: crates/toastty-render/src/tgp/theme_tint.rs (new, CPU-resolvable resolver) + viewport RenderOpts.theme_tint (default false): when on, multiply the terminal's active DEFAULT-FOREGROUND color (read once per frame, linearized) into the default material's diffuse base, as a pre-lighting material-INPUT stage (§11.1 ordering, strength fixed 1.0 in v1). Applies ONLY to MaterialId 0 (default-material) nodes whose per-node tint is the neutral default white [255,255,255,255]; a node with an explicit non-white tint is left untouched; never touches PBR nodes or registered material baseColor. effective_diffuse_linear = base_linear × lerp(white, fg_linear, 1.0). Expose Term::tgp_node_effective_diffuse(vp, node) → [f32;3] computed CPU-side so the stage is testable without a GPU.
